key_insight: A spectrally regularized latent compression stage dramatically improves flow-matching turbulence generation by preserving dissipation-range structure that standard MSE-trained VAEs tend to suppress.
engineering_relevance: This yields a much better fidelity-vs-sampling-cost tradeoff for synthetic turbulence surrogates, enabling more accurate generation with far fewer function evaluations.
method: Replace the MSE-trained VAE with a spectrally regularized latent compressor using a zone-weighted log-spectral loss.
Train a latent flow matching model on the compressed representation for unconditional turbulence generation.
Use encoder-decoder and support-amplitude ablations to isolate whether improvements come from latent organization or decoder capacity.
evidence_signal: On a 256^2 DNS dataset at Re_f ≈ 2250, deep-dissipation retained spectral power improves from 25% to 94% in reconstruction and from 20% to 79% in unconditional generation, with DD bias reaching -0.117 at 20 function evaluations.
watch_item: The model still shows a residual gap in the magnitude of S_3, indicating that phase-coherent triadic organization remains unresolved.
paper_title: Spectrally Regularized Latent Flow Matching for Turbulence Generation
